name: CheckLink upstream lock
how_to_read: vendored: bytes (or data compiled from them) ship in the app. Each records its exact version, source address, size, sha256 (and the npm sha512 integrity for packages), licence, and how it was checked against the registry or upstream.
node tools/vendor.mjs --check proves the files in the repository still match this lock, offline; node --test tests/ runs it.
commit pins the exact upstream revision; for rule sources, the revision whose file matches the copy read on 2026-10-10 (matched by git blob hash unless notes say otherwise).

role: vendored = bytes ship in the app; derived = the app ships data Stormberry wrote from it; seed or checked-against = rule facts compared against it; facts-only = read to check facts, nothing copied (GPL and LGPL sources stay in this group).
upstream_changed_since_pin: true means the file had newer commits than the pin when it was read; the rule-update report should diff them.
Nothing here is fetched at build or run time. The rule sources and search research entries were recorded by the research pass of 2026-10-10 and are carried over unchanged.
search_research_files: the research summaries in rules/research/, each with the sha256 of the archive file it was copied from and of the copy, and what was taken out of it.

vendored.what: QR and barcode decoder: zxing-cpp compiled to WebAssembly, reader build only, run in a Web Worker (src/qr-worker.js)
vendored.release_age_rule: 14 days (spec section 4). 3.1.4 is the newest release that meets it on 2026-10-11. 3.1.5 (published 2026-10-06, with upstream decoding and security fixes) meets it from 2026-10-20: swap with node tools/vendor.mjs --zxing <tarball> and update this entry.
vendored.integrity_checked: 2026-10-11: the tarball was downloaded from the registry and its sha512 equals the registry's dist.integrity above
vendored.provenance: https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/zxing-wasm@3.1.4 (SLSA v1): built from commit ba54ad0bba3f2e230c0f0a503d8d71065ef39c30, the commit the tag v3.1.4 points to; the attestation names the ref as refs/heads/main at that commit, not the tag itself
vendored.licence: MIT (wrapper and its JavaScript); the .wasm also contains zxing-cpp and the zxing-wasm C++ binding (Apache-2.0), libzueci (BSD-3-Clause), stb_image (MIT or Unlicense) and the Emscripten runtime: Emscripten (MIT or NCSA), musl libc (MIT), LLVM libc++, libc++abi and compiler-rt (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception). Texts in licences/.

wasm.how: base64 inside an ES module (export default '<base64>'), handed to the decoder as wasmBinary; the vendored reader carries the same hash as ZXING_WASM_SHA256

notes: dist/es/reader/index.js imports only ../share.js. share.js holds the default locateFile, which builds https://fastly.jsdelivr.net/npm/zxing-wasm@3.1.4/dist/... addresses; CheckLink passes wasmBinary and its own locateFile, so that default is never used, and src/qr-worker.js removes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and EventSource from the worker before the decoder loads.
Runtime dependencies listed by npm (type-fest, @types/emscripten) are TypeScript types only; nothing from them ships.

stb_image is fetched by zxing-cpp's CMake (FetchContent of https://github.com/nothings/stb, no commit pinned), so the exact stb commit inside the .wasm is not recorded upstream; its licence block was taken from stb_image.h at commit 013ac3beddff3dbffafd5177e7972067cd2b5083 (the latest change to that file, 2024-05-31).

Deploy-time change, not made here: the page's meta policy gains 'wasm-unsafe-eval' in script-src and worker-src 'self'; a worker takes its policy only from its own response headers, so check.stormberry.as also needs a host-scoped Cloudflare response-header rule (action Set) whose Content-Security-Policy allows 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. tests/serve.py sends the recommended header; NOTICE gives it in full.

conversion.how: node tools/vendor.mjs --qrcodegen <typescript-5.9.3.tgz>: the compiler from the tarball (checked against the integrity below) runs ts.transpileModule on the pinned file with compiler_options, which takes the types out and turns each namespace into a function, as upstream's build.sh does with tsc --strict --target ES6. tools/vendor.mjs puts its own header before the output and one line, export default qrcodegen;, after it. Nothing else changes. node tools/vendor.mjs --check proves the header, the output (output_sha256) and the export line without the compiler.

tool.integrity_checked: 2026-10-11: the tarball was downloaded from the registry and its sha512 equals the registry's dist.integrity above
tool.why_this_version: a build tool, run once by a person; nothing from it ships. 5.9.3 is the last 5.x release, more than a year past the 14-day rule; npm's latest on 2026-10-11 is 7.0.2

notes: No official npm package exists, so the file is pinned by commit, like the word lists and the domain list.

The encoder writes text as UTF-8 bytes (byte mode) when it is not all digits or capitals. CheckLink writes the host in its xn-- form first, so only a path or query with letters outside English goes in as UTF-8, and then with the ECI marker 26 (UTF-8) in front (src/qr-make.js makeQr): without it, ZBar 0.23.93 read 2 of 4 such codes as Shift JIS or GBK on 11 October 2026. Plain ASCII never carries the marker.
third_party/ is not published; the converted file in vendor/ ships with the website and the app, in a folder named with the commit, so a new commit is a new address and the file carries no ?v= stamp.

vendored.what: Unicode's confusables.txt (UTS #39): which characters can pass for which. CheckLink keeps the characters whose prototype is plain ASCII once combining marks are taken off, for its look-alike checks (stage 3): names written in letters of another alphabet, hyphen, slash and dot look-alikes, and look-alikes of the brands in src/brands.js.
vendored.licence: Unicode-3.0 (licences/Unicode-3.0.txt; the copyright notice is repeated at the top of src/confusables.js)
vendored.upstream_check: 2026-10-11: downloaded again from the versioned address above and from https://www.unicode.org/Public/security/latest/confusables.txt; both gave these exact bytes (the same sha256 as the copy read on 2026-10-10).
notes: The versioned path moved under /Public/18.0.0/security/; /Public/security/18.0.0/ returns 404.

The spec (section 4) estimated 1,855 entries for the ASCII subset; 2,269 entries have a target that is plain ASCII as written, and 2,561 once combining marks are taken off the target (so that, for example, the slashed o counts as o). CheckLink keeps the 2,561.
